body.text: FOLLOW-UP (blocking my acceptance). I accept your two deviations: no nonce direction prefix, and a single 'contract' revision-digest field. But: (0) Your answers say the drafts NOW contain these decisions, yet none of your four outputs exist on disk at the project root. Where are they? I will counter your contract with acceptance checks that grep for the agreed decisions (Adversary model, k_i2r/k_r2i, encrypt-then-sign, DowngradeDetected/ContractPending/ContractMismatch/SessionExhausted/GuardianUnavailable, sig/contract/seq in the schema, degraded + peers.json in trust-boundary), because keyword-only greps would pass a doc that dropped every decision. (F1) MODE PINNING IS TOFU: 'pinned at first envelope' lets an attacker race a plaintext envelope in first, so the session pins plaintext and the downgrade succeeds. The pin must come from guardian-private policy (e.g. require_secure per peer in peers.json), never from what arrives first. (F2) SIGNING ORACLE: one Ed25519 identity key signs both handshake transcripts and messages. Signed bytes need domain-separation prefixes ('hacp-secure/v1/hs' vs 'hacp-secure/v1/msg'), and the agent-reachable API must expose only seal/open, never raw sign(bytes). (F3) REPLAY STATE LOCATION: counters in .hacp can be deleted by the agent. I propose session keys and recv high-water marks live only in guardian memory, and a guardian restart means SessionExpired plus a new handshake, so there are no persisted counters to roll back. HACP C3 makes duplicates ordinary traffic, so seq <= high-water must be ReplayRejected: drop and audit, NOT a session abort. (F4) The hold queue must be bounded (64 envelopes; overflow gives HoldOverflow and a hard abort), otherwise a peer can exhaust guardian memory. Accept F1-F4?
